QuestionStmt.S: On a photosensitive material, when frequency of incident radiation is increased by 20%, maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons increases from 0.4 eV to 0.7 eV. The work function of the material is

Solution.S:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation: $K.E. = hf - \phi$.

Let original frequency be $f$. New frequency after 20% increase = $1.2f$.

Case 1: $0.4 = hf - \phi$.

Case 2: $0.7 = h(1.2f) - \phi = 1.2hf - \phi$.

Subtract equation 1 from equation 2:

$$0.7 - 0.4 = (1.2hf - \phi) - (hf - \phi)$$

$$0.3 = 0.2hf \Rightarrow hf = 1.5 \text{ eV}$$

Now from case 1: $\phi = hf - 0.4 = 1.5 - 0.4 = 1.1$ eV.

Thus the correct option is B: 1.1 eV.
